head: cloud/bench-tp2-interrupt-cleanup
title: fix(bench): stop both TP2 ranks when startup is interrupted
body:
> AI disclosure: I am not a software developer. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) developed and tested this patch; an independent Claude Fable 5.1 review approved it before submission; this is not a claim of human developer review. Claude Code cloud session, CPU only, no GPU testing.

Test scope (CPU build/tests only, cloud VM, no GPU, no RDMA, no second host): `python3 -I tests/tools/serving_bench_test.py` and `ctest --preset cpu-test -R '^serving_bench_test$'` pass on this branch (based on `rdma` fbaf343). The new check fails without the change, separately for `Server` and for `Tp2Server`. `tools/ci/check-docs.py` passes. The model bench itself was not run.

## Problem

`Server.start` and `Tp2Server.start` in `tools/gufo/model_bench/servers.py` stop their processes only on `Exception`. Both start their children with `start_new_session=True`, so a Ctrl-C in the terminal reaches only the bench script. Pressing it while the ranks load (`wait_ready` can wait for minutes) raises `KeyboardInterrupt`, which is not an `Exception`. And because `__enter__` raised, `__exit__` never runs. The local rank-0 container, the ssh client and the remote rank-1 container keep running. They hold both GPUs and the fixed bootstrap and control ports, so the next bench run fails until they are removed by hand.

## Change

- Both `start` methods catch `BaseException`. Cleanup is otherwise unchanged: the same `stop()` runs (remote cleanup over ssh, then local), and the interrupt is re-raised.
- `tests/tools/serving_bench_test.py` patches the spawns and makes `wait_ready` raise `KeyboardInterrupt`. It then checks that the interrupt propagates and that `stop` ran once, for `Server` and for `Tp2Server`.

Built in a cloud session (CPU only); Strix Halo validation pending.

review.summary: Two-line BaseException fix with a reproducible regression test; claims match evidence, disclosure and scope are exact, target branch is right. Approve.
